gameOver.message: Player MiMo Stoic is the winner

annotations.description: With Deep-Cavern Bat's trigger, MiMo Stoic chose to exile Archdruid's Charm over Surrak, Elusive Hunter. While Archdruid's Charm is a versatile card, Surrak is a 4/3 with trample that can't be countered and draws cards when targeted by opponent's spells - making it very difficult to remove efficiently. MiMo Stoic has two copies of Shoot the Sheriff in hand, which can destroy Icetill Explorer (non-outlaw) but notably cannot destroy Surrak (who is a Warrior, not an outlaw, so actually Shoot the Sheriff CAN hit him). However, Surrak's 'draw a card when targeted' ability means using Shoot the Sheriff on him gives the opponent card advantage. Meanwhile, Archdruid's Charm, while flexible, is a triple-green spell that the opponent may not be able to cast early. The opponent has only one Forest and a Sazh's Chocobo on board - they need two more green sources for Archdruid's Charm. Surrak only needs one more green source (2G) and represents immediate board pressure. Taking Surrak would have been slightly better as it's the most threatening card that punishes removal.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Archdruid's Charm from opponent's hand with Deep-Cavern Bat
annotations.betterLine: Exile Surrak, Elusive Hunter - it's a must-answer threat that punishes targeted removal (drawing cards), has trample, and can't be countered. Archdruid's Charm requires triple green which the opponent may struggle to cast soon.

annotations.description: Sazh's Chocobo received a +1/+1 counter from landfall when Forest entered on turn 1, making it a 1/2. The opponent has a Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 with flying/lifelink) as their only creature. Attacking with the 1/2 Chocobo is free damage - the Bat has flying so it can block, but the opponent is unlikely to block with their valuable Deep-Cavern Bat (which is exiling a card from Qwen3L's hand) since trading a 1/1 flyer for 1 damage prevention is poor. Even if blocked, the Chocobo would kill the Bat (1 power vs 1 toughness) and the Bat would deal 1 to Chocobo (leaving it at 1 toughness), resulting in a trade that frees the exiled card. Either way - free damage or getting back the exiled card - attacking is strictly better than not attacking.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Sazh's Chocobo
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Sazh's Chocobo. If unblocked, deal 1 damage. If blocked by Deep-Cavern Bat, both trade and the exiled card returns to hand. Both outcomes are favorable.

annotations.description: Playing Forest instead of Fabled Passage misses value with Sazh's Chocobo. Fabled Passage would sacrifice and fetch a basic land, triggering Chocobo's landfall twice (once when the fetched land enters), giving it two +1/+1 counters instead of one. With only 2 lands in play, the fetched land would enter tapped, but since this is the postcombat main phase, the tapped land doesn't matter this turn. The extra counter on Chocobo is meaningful value.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest from hand, getting one landfall trigger on Sazh's Chocobo.
annotations.betterLine: Play Fabled Passage, sacrifice it to fetch a basic Forest. This triggers Sazh's Chocobo landfall twice (once for the fetched land entering), netting an extra +1/+1 counter. Save the Forest in hand for next turn's land drop.

annotations.description: Casting Kaito precombat means he enters as a 3/4 creature during MiMo's turn. Deep-Cavern Bat could attack first, and if unblocked, Kaito could be ninjutsu'd in (though the mana cost is the same at 1UB). However, the main issue is sequencing: by casting Kaito precombat, MiMo loses the option to attack with Deep-Cavern Bat first and then decide whether to use Kaito's ninjutsu ability (returning the bat to hand to replay it and exile another card) or cast Kaito post-combat. Attacking with the bat first gives more information and flexibility. If the bat is unblocked, ninjutsu-ing Kaito in would return the bat to hand (to be replayed later for another hand look) AND Kaito would deal combat damage, enabling his 0 ability to draw a card. This is significantly better than just casting Kaito from hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kaito, Bane of Nightmares precombat from hand
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Deep-Cavern Bat first. If unblocked, use Kaito's Ninjutsu ({1}{U}{B}) to put him onto the battlefield tapped and attacking, dealing combat damage and enabling his 0 loyalty ability to draw a card (since the opponent would have lost life). This also returns Deep-Cavern Bat to hand for reuse.

annotations.description: Not attacking with Kaito (a 3/4 hexproof creature during your turn) into an empty board, missing 3 free damage. The opponent has no creatures to block, and Kaito has hexproof so he can't be targeted by removal. This leaves 3 damage on the table for no reason.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 flying lifelink)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Deep-Cavern Bat and Kaito to deal 4 total damage instead of 1, then use Kaito's 0 ability post-combat for surveil 2 + draw 1 (since opponent lost life).

annotations.description: With 4 lands (2 Forests + 2 Fabled Passages) and Surrak costing {2}{G}, the player should be able to cast Surrak. Even if the interface didn't offer it directly, the player should have activated a Fabled Passage first to fetch a Forest (getting to 3 Forests + 1 Passage), which might have enabled the cast. Activating Fabled Passage with 4+ lands untaps the fetched land, so they'd have 3 untapped lands to cast Surrak. Instead they passed without developing their board at all, missing a land drop and a creature deployment on a critical turn 4 where the opponent has Kaito threatening to generate value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Fabled Passage or casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Activate a Fabled Passage to fetch a Forest (untapped since 4+ lands), then cast Surrak, Elusive Hunter for {2}{G}. This develops a 4/3 trampler that punishes opponent's targeted removal with card draw, pressuring Kaito.

annotations.description: MiMo Stoic intended to use Kaito's 0 ability (Surveil 2, then draw a card for each opponent who lost life this turn) but instead activated the +1 ability, getting a Ninja emblem. Since Kaito is the only Ninja on the battlefield, the emblem provides minimal value compared to Surveil 2 + potential card draw (the opponent lost 9 life this turn from combat, so the 0 ability would have drawn a card). The +1 emblem is a long-term investment but the 0 ability providing surveil 2 and a card draw was significantly better this turn, especially since Kaito already dealt combat damage meaning the opponent lost life this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Kaito's +1 loyalty ability, getting an emblem that gives Ninjas +1/+1.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Kaito's 0 loyalty ability to Surveil 2 and draw a card (since the opponent lost life this turn from Kaito's combat damage). This would improve hand quality and provide card advantage rather than a marginal stat buff.

annotations.description: Tishana's Tidebinder has Flash and a reactive ETB (counter an activated/triggered ability), but was cast during MiMo Stoic's own postcombat main with nothing to counter. The opponent has Fabled Passages that could be activated, and could play threats with relevant abilities next turn. Holding the Tidebinder for the opponent's turn would preserve the option to counter something meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tishana's Tidebinder during own postcombat main phase with no ability to counter
annotations.betterLine: Hold Tishana's Tidebinder to cast on opponent's turn with Flash, potentially countering a Fabled Passage activation or an ETB/triggered ability from whatever the opponent plays. Could instead cast Enduring Curiosity (also has Flash) or simply pass with mana open.

annotations.description: Tishana's Tidebinder's ETB trigger was targeted at itself (its own ETB ability on the stack), effectively countering its own ability and accomplishing nothing. The Tidebinder's ability should have either been used to counter a meaningful opponent ability or simply declined (targeting nothing). By targeting its own trigger, the Tidebinder lost all its abilities permanently (since it countered an ability of a creature - itself - it loses all abilities as long as it remains on the battlefield), making it a vanilla 3/2 that can never use its ability again.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Tishana's Tidebinder's own ETB ability with itself, countering its own ability and causing it to lose all abilities permanently.
annotations.betterLine: Decline to counter any ability (choose no target / target nothing), preserving Tishana's Tidebinder as a 3/2 body without self-inflicted drawback. There appear to be no opponent abilities on the stack worth countering, so the ETB should have been allowed to resolve without a target.

annotations.description: With 2 Forests and 2 Fabled Passages, activating Fabled Passage first (getting an untapped Forest since 4+ lands) would give 3 green mana, enabling Surrak, Elusive Hunter (4/3 trample, uncounterable, draws on targeting) which is significantly stronger than Badgermole Cub (2/2). The correct sequencing is Fabled Passage activation first, then cast Surrak.
annotations.actionTaken: Likely cast Badgermole Cub (2/2 for 1G) without first activating Fabled Passage to unlock stronger plays
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fabled Passage to fetch a Forest (enters untapped with 4+ lands), then cast Surrak, Elusive Hunter for 2G - a much more impactful 4/3 trample creature that can't be countered

annotations.description: Qwen3L Spike should play a land before casting spells this turn. They have Fabled Passage in hand and could play it first, then sacrifice it to fetch a basic land. This would give them an additional land on the battlefield. Playing Badgermole Cub first before playing a land is a sequencing error - especially since Badgermole Cub's earthbend ability targets a land you control (more lands = more options), and playing the land first could matter for triggering landfall or having more mana available post-combat. Additionally, casting a creature before combat when holding no combat tricks is generally suboptimal - they should enter combat first with any existing creatures, then cast creatures in second main phase to deny the opponent information.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Badgermole Cub before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Fabled Passage first (potentially sacrificing it to fetch a Forest), then cast Badgermole Cub in the precombat or post-combat main phase to maximize mana and earthbend targets.

annotations.description: Earthbending Fabled Passage instead of a Forest wastes a valuable fetchland. With 3 Icetill Explorers in hand that have landfall triggers, Fabled Passage's ability to fetch basics and trigger landfall is much more valuable than a basic Forest. The earthbended land becomes a creature that could die to removal, and while earthbend returns it tapped, the fetchland utility is better preserved un-earthbended.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose untapped Fabled Passage as the earthbend target for Badgermole Cub
annotations.betterLine: Earthbend a tapped Forest instead, preserving Fabled Passage for future land searching and landfall triggers with the Icetill Explorers in hand

annotations.description: Attacked with only the animated Fabled Passage (1/1) instead of also attacking with Badgermole Cub (2/2). The opponent has only Tishana's Tidebinder (3/2) untapped as a blocker, so attacking with both creatures would guarantee at least one gets through for damage. Being at 11 life vs opponent's 21, maximizing damage output is important.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only the animated Fabled Passage land creature (1/1)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Badgermole Cub and the animated Fabled Passage to force the opponent to choose which to block, guaranteeing some damage gets through

annotations.description: Only attacked with Kaito when Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 flying, lifelink) could safely attack as well since the opponent has no flyers to block it. This is free damage + lifegain with zero risk. Tishana's Tidebinder could also likely attack safely since the opponent only has one ground blocker (Badgermole Cub), meaning at most one of Kaito/Tidebinder gets blocked.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Kaito, Bane of Nightmares
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (Deep-Cavern Bat, Kaito, and Tishana's Tidebinder). Deep-Cavern Bat is unblockable flying damage + lifelink. With only one blocker, the opponent can block at most one ground creature, guaranteeing at least 4 damage instead of 3.

annotations.description: At 11 life facing 8 damage from three attackers (Kaito 4/5, Tidebinder 3/2, Deep-Cavern Bat 1/1), the player only blocked with Badgermole Cub instead of also using the earthbent Fabled Passage. The earthbent land returns to the battlefield tapped when it dies, so blocking with it costs almost nothing. Using both blockers (Cub on Tidebinder to trade, Passage on Kaito to absorb 4 damage) would reduce damage taken from 5 to 1, preserving 4 crucial life points at a low life total.
annotations.actionTaken: Only assigned Badgermole Cub as a blocker, likely taking 5 damage (blocking Tidebinder) or 4 damage (blocking Kaito), going to 6-7 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block with both Badgermole Cub (on Tidebinder, trading) and earthbent Fabled Passage (on Kaito, chump blocking). Take only 1 damage from Deep-Cavern Bat, staying at 10 life. The Fabled Passage returns to battlefield tapped as a land when it dies.

annotations.description: Casting Llanowar Elves (costs G) before playing a land drop is suboptimal sequencing. With Fabled Passage in hand, playing the Fabled Passage first (which enters untapped and can be sacrificed to find a basic Forest, untapping it since they control 4+ lands) would give an additional mana source this turn. This would allow casting a 4-drop like Icetill Explorer or Surrak this turn instead of just the Elves. At 6 life facing a board with Kaito and Enduring Curiosity, maximizing mana development this turn is critical - playing land first, then potentially casting both Llanowar Elves AND a bigger threat would be significantly better than just deploying the Elves.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Llanowar Elves before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Fabled Passage first, sacrifice it to find a basic Forest (untapped since controlling 4+ lands), giving 5 mana available. Then cast Icetill Explorer (2GG) or Surrak (2G) as a more impactful play, or cast Llanowar Elves plus another spell.

annotations.description: MiMo Stoic has lethal on board with Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 flying), Kaito (3/4 as creature during their turn), and Enduring Curiosity (4/3) for 8 total damage against opponent at 6 life. Opponent only has Llanowar Elves (1/1) to block. Even if Llanowar Elves blocks one ground creature, flying Deep-Cavern Bat + the other attacker is enough. Instead, they cast a second legendary Kaito, triggering the legend rule and wasting a card.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast a second Kaito, Bane of Nightmares from hand during precombat main phase, triggering the legend rule.
annotations.betterLine: Go directly to combat and attack with Deep-Cavern Bat, Kaito, and Enduring Curiosity for 8 damage, which is lethal against the opponent at 6 life.

annotations.description: MiMo Stoic has lethal on board with Deep-Cavern Bat (1) + Kaito (3) + Enduring Curiosity (4) = 8 damage against opponent at 6 life. Even if opponent blocks with Llanowar Elves, at minimum 7 damage gets through. Casting Bitter Triumph (requiring a discard or 3 life) to remove the blocker is unnecessary.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bitter Triumph to remove Llanowar Elves before combat, paying additional cost of discarding a card or 3 life.
annotations.betterLine: Skip straight to combat and attack with all three creatures for lethal damage. Even through a Llanowar Elves block, 7+ damage gets through against opponent's 6 life. If removal was desired, Requiting Hex ({B}) or Shoot the Sheriff ({1}{B}) would be more efficient.

annotations.description: Chose to blight Deep-Cavern Bat, which killed it (1/1 with -1/-1 counter = 0/0) and returned the exiled Archdruid's Charm to the opponent's hand. The blight cost was optional ('you may'), and even if paying it, Kaito (3/4→2/3) or Enduring Curiosity (4/3→3/2) would have been far better targets since they survive the counter. Giving back Archdruid's Charm to an opponent for 2 life gain is a terrible trade.
annotations.actionTaken: Put the -1/-1 counter on Deep-Cavern Bat, killing it and returning Archdruid's Charm to opponent's hand.
annotations.betterLine: Either don't pay the blight cost at all, or if paying it, put the -1/-1 counter on Enduring Curiosity (4/3→3/2) or Kaito (3/4→2/3) who both survive the counter without releasing exiled cards.

annotations.description: Discarded Soulstone Sanctuary instead of Swamp for Bitter Triumph's additional cost. Soulstone Sanctuary has a creature-land activation ability ({4}: becomes a 3/3 vigilance creature) which gives it more utility than a basic Swamp, especially with 8 lands already on board making the activation cost easy to pay.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Soulstone Sanctuary
annotations.betterLine: Discard Swamp instead, preserving the utility land that can become a 3/3 creature with vigilance for closing out the game or providing extra pressure.

annotations.description: Discarded Bitterbloom Bearer, a strong card advantage engine that creates flying tokens each upkeep, when less valuable options were available. While the opponent is at 6 life and MiMo is far ahead, Bitterbloom Bearer provides evasive pressure to close the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Bitterbloom Bearer
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Swamp (basic land) or the duplicate Shoot the Sheriff (already have one in hand), preserving the more impactful creature for potential future use.

annotations.description: With the opponent at 6 life, choosing Island over Restless Reef misses the opportunity to add a creature-land that could help close the game. Restless Reef can become a 4/4 deathtouch creature for {2}{U}{B}, and combined with Kaito's attack next turn, would likely represent lethal damage. It also still produces U or B mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Island (basic land)
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Restless Reef - it enters tapped (fine since it's during combat and all lands are tapped anyway), produces U/B mana, and represents a 4/4 deathtouch threat that combined with Kaito could deliver lethal to the opponent at 6 life next turn.

annotations.description: At 6 opponent life with a strong board position, choosing a basic Swamp over Restless Reef (a 4/4 deathtouch creature-land that can close the game) or Fountainport (which provides card draw and token generation utility) wastes significant value. Restless Reef in particular would be a potent threat to close out the game against a 6-life opponent with an empty board.
annotations.actionTaken: Played basic Swamp as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Restless Reef (enters tapped but provides a powerful 4/4 deathtouch creature-land to close the game) or Fountainport for utility if wanting an untapped land.
